= Basic Cache Operations with the .NET Client
:summary: Connect to an Infinispan Server and perform basic cache operations with the .NET Hot Rod client
:mode: remote
:topics: caching,getting-started
:keywords: cache,put,get,remove,dotnet,csharp
:duration: 5
:source-dir: non-java-clients/c#/cache

TIP: The source code for this tutorial is available on link:https://github.com/infinispan/infinispan-simple-tutorials/tree/main/{source-dir}[GitHub].

This tutorial demonstrates how to connect to an Infinispan server and perform basic cache operations using the .NET Hot Rod client.

== Prerequisites

* A running Infinispan server.
* .NET 10 or later.

== Running the Example

[source,shell]
----
dotnet run --project cache
----

== Code Walkthrough

=== Connecting to the Server

The example connects to the Infinispan server using a Hot Rod URI.
You can override the default URI by setting the `INFINISPAN_URI` environment variable.

[source,csharp]
----
var client = InfinispanClient.FromUri("hotrod://admin:password@localhost:11222");
----

=== Creating the Cache

The example creates a cache using the administration API.

[source,csharp]
----
await admin.GetOrCreateCache("test");
----

=== Storing and Retrieving Entries

Use `Put` to store a key-value pair and `Get` to retrieve it.

[source,csharp]
----
await cache.Put("key", "value");
var result = await cache.Get("key");
----

== Expected Output

[source]
----
Cache 'test' ready.
key = value
Cache removed.
----
